newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Kurdish factions pledge immediate truce.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Kurdish factions pledge immediate truce.

text.p: The two Kurdish factions fighting in Northern Iraq pledged to observe a ceasefire from 5 p.m. EDT (2100 GMT) on Wednesday, the U.S. State Department said.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said the agreement followed contacts on Wednesday by the United States, Britain and Turkey with the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).

"Both parties have given commitments to begin the ceasefire at midnight tonight, October 23, Iraq time," Burns said in a statement. "We call on both parties to honour those commitments, to repeat them publicly, and to place their forces in defensive postures."
The U.S. statement was issued after the ceasefire was supposed to come into force, and there was no immediate word from the region on whether the warring factions were observing it.

Burns noted that Assistant Secretary of State Robert Pelletreau, who held separate talks with KDP and PUK leaders in Turkey this week, said in Ankara on Wednesday morning both factions had agreed in principle to an immediate ceasefire.

"Fighting in the region continued last night, and the ceasefire did not take hold as expected," he said. This indicated the ceasefire had originally been meant to start on Tuesday night and had been pushed back 24 hours.

Burns' statement called on Iran and Iraq to avoid actions that could make the process of Kurdish reconciliation more difficult and worsen tensions in the region -- an obvious appeal to them not to intervene in the fighting.
The latest spate of fighting began on Aug. 31, when Iraqi troops and tanks helped the KDP capture the city of Arbil from the PUK, prompting a retaliatory U.S. missile strike against Iraq.

The United States evacuated most of its employees in the area, as well as the military command centre of an allied force that has been protecting the Kurdish region of Iraq since Baghdad's defeat in the 1991 Gulf War.
While the KDP has made no secret of the assistance it has received from Iraq, the PUK and the Iranian government have denied KDP allegations that Tehran is aiding the PUK with troops and munitions.
Hours after Pelletreau ended his talks on Tuesday, there were reports of new skirmishes, with the PUK of Jalal Talabani capturing the towns of Ranya and Koy Sanjak from Massoud Barzani's KDP.
Pelletreau flew from Turkey to Dubai in the United Arab Emirates on Wednesday at the start of a tour of Gulf states.
But before leaving, he said U.S., British and Turkish representatives planned further meetings with delegations from each Kurdish group in Ankara next week.
Burns said Pelletreau himself would return to Turkey to chair those meetings.
Many cease-fires between the two groups have been called and broken since fighting first flared up in late 1994.
Washington encouraged the Kurds to split from Baghdad after the Gulf War but has been powerless to stop a power struggle between the two Kurdish groups that has divided the mountainous region.
